record_notes.DCP-LETT-1044: Sunday, conjectural 1847 from watermark and frequent London visits. A watermark supplies a lower dating clue, not proof the paper was used that year; no exact meeting date follows. Asks half an hour on Tuesday between half past twelve and half past one, confirmed in raw MathML, to discuss unnamed zoological points. Caroline Owen January 7 recollection in apparatus is a separate visit, not identification of this Tuesday appointment. No preserved incoming prompt or accomplished meeting.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1061: February 12 with supplied 1847 year. Received Muñiz letter and papers after almost four months lying in London, not four months in Darwin possession. Offers fossils through College; Darwin initially understands gift rather than sale, asks missing Megatherium parts list, shipping expenses, publications and encouragement. Machairodus identity is his hypothesis, later Smilodon classification editorial. Spanish newspaper paper has arrived, English translation still planned; asks Paris shipment news. Owen fish lectures first chapter read, not all chapters until later March record. Acasta application declined because fresh British specimens obtained. Missing Muñiz letter and Owen suggestion cannot be recreated; later 1063 identifies the August 30 input but is another outgoing witness. Museum minute summary of purchase is not sufficient to override later uncompleted negotiation evidence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-938: Saturday evening assigned March 6, 1847, the earliest possible Saturday after Shrewsbury return; rationale does not by itself independently prove this precise day. Last letters crossed; missing Owen response and Morris information resolve prior mistaken gift assumption. Now sends Morris translation and original Spanish of Muñiz fossil paper, asks anatomical evaluation, guaranteed offer and possible publication of measurements. Translation quality doubted because translator not anatomist; plans and advocacy are not completed sale or publication. Scarlet-fever pamphlet sent to library. Later 1853 offer discussion in executor note must not be imported into 1847. Translation manuscripts reportedly survive elsewhere, but their text and original Muñiz letter are absent from this preserved collection.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13833: Incomplete closing fragment, recipient Owen likely from manuscript notation but uncorroborated. Reference to Hooker India expedition supports broad November 1847–1851 window crossing current period; preserve it. Opening I had not heard was presumably inserted by Owen and is absent from retained Darwin text, which begins before. Whewell scolding is reported, educational-reform explanation conjectural; no full incoming Owen communication. Expected Hooker novelties are future expectations, not completed return knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13834: December 23 in one of eight years 1847–1854, encoded as discrete alternatives, not an arbitrary day in continuous interval. Queries tooth possibly left with Owen and recalls uncertain Searles Wood request one or two years before; Owen vague recollection and Christmas wishes imply missing incoming communication. Corrects FitzRoy exaggeration about glacier wave from Darwin own voyage memory. Related 1852–1853 unknown-correspondent letter is an editorial possibility, not proof of year. No current-period assignment or physical location of tooth established.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1150: Friday night assigned February 4, 1848. Auckland/Herschel request arrived this morning; asks whether previously sent coral remarks belong under geology, given new commission. Original invitation asks Owens to come following Saturday week, with travel logistics. P5 begins after Owen refusal note just received; distinguish this later-in-composition input from morning commission, no proof either arrived before opening prose. Raw MathML departure is quarter past four, not 14. Actual later visit and published division of coral content are editorial outcomes, not yet agreed in this text. Both incoming notes and original coral manuscript are missing.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1166: Sunday assigned March 26, 1848. Offers unsolicited microscope advice, uncertain whether Owen instructions already submitted. Large fixed stage holding three-inch saucer is key advantage over old Beagle instrument; distinguishes Brown recommendation, Chevalier model and Smith/Beck manufacture. Offers fuller description, not proof enclosure already sent. Oral talk at Down is past, next London meeting prospective after illness. Silence to be interpreted as advice superfluous is a historical requested convention, not actual assent or an agent instruction. Later advertising, Lubbock ownership and manual editions are separate apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-997: Incomplete published quotation, conjectural April 1848, correcting printed 1843 date through book/publication context. It is Darwin Coral reefs that Owen praised, not an Owen coral volume. Darwin has read parts of Owen archetype report that he could follow, urges repeated labels on every woodcut for accessibility. The recommendation for voyagers may be in manuscript/communication before 1849 manual publication; no exact incoming personal text is preserved. Bracketed useful and ellipses remain source interventions/gaps. Not a reply to Darwin own microscope letters.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1167F: Sunday assigned April 2, 1848 through fortnight since geology submission and planned London call, not a wholly independent exact date. Sends expanded microscope advice as separate notes, allows editorial cuts, credits actual Hooker dissection experience and Hooker/Brown lens recommendations. The geology manuscript believed lost at Admiralty is a different item, sent about fortnight earlier. Requests quarter-hour Wednesday talk and examination of Thompson book/Goadby preparations; planned inspection is not already-read evidence. Thanks Owen synopsis headings and hopes for print. Later published text, edition changes and probable Ibla topic remain editorial. No preserved incoming request or microscope enclosure text here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1089: Tuesday, conjectural 1849 based on mourning stationery. Acts on earlier invitation to tea, potentially oral; proposes Thursday 7½ oclock, confirmed MathML, conditional on convenience and stomach. Absence by eight would signify illness. Silence convention and proposed visit do not prove Owen reply or actual attendance. No exact date or incoming text supplied by broad year.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1228: Saturday assigned February 24, 1849. Thanks missing Owen note and C. hunteri but carrier failed Thursday; Monday collection is prospective and specimen location uncertain between College and Society. Gratitude does not prove physical specimen receipt. Raw MathML says four-fifths of time lost to illness, not 45. Water cure intended for early summer, actual earlier Malvern arrival is future relative to this plan. Sulivan assistance reported through Owen, not original Sulivan letter. Limbs book ordered, not yet read; own peduncle/shell homology finding is current. Diddleus log-book jest refers reported sea-serpent controversy, separate from missing correspondence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1231: Tuesday in assigned January–March 23, 1850 window based on reading notes, not exact date or proof January 1 lower composition. Thanks Owen handling Ehrenberg parcel and sends reimbursement stamps; exact parcel contents/receipt and Owen cover missing. Limbs only mid-read now, Parthenogenesis read some time ago. A later reading-log entry for both on March 23 cannot erase these distinct states or make both first known that day.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1322: April 28 with supplied 1850 year. Recent missing Sulivan letter from Falklands asks vessel, November expedition and six-week route via Gallegos/St Julian/Bahia Blanca, without salary; fallback £150–200 charter unaffordable. Darwin asks Owen to prompt Beaufort, plans to reply, expects society help unlikely. This current logistical request is not preserved 1845 fossil-discovery letter 730. Thanks prior missing Owen introduction to Mrs Dixon but declines Worthing journey; renews exact plate XXVIII figure 9 Xiphidium request from 1357. Prospectus already sent; hoped lectures publication never completed according to later apparatus. No acquired specimen or successful expedition inferred.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1357: Friday before April 28, 1850, upper constraint inferred from same plate XXVIII figure 9 request in 1322. Late Mr Dixon and independently supplied 1849 death in 1355 apparatus support a derived 1849–April 27, 1850 window while retaining original open XML lower bound and date uncertainty. Requests this valve and previously discussed figures 3/4; Owen offer to borrow may have been oral or missing correspondence. Conditional favourable answer requested, not actual successful loan. Both this and 1322 are Darwin outgoing; no QA edge between them.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1355: September 10 with supplied 1850 year. Requests Dixon cirripede proof sheets; plates have been shown by Sowerby, but prose not yet received/read and volume not published until December. Darwin own fossil volume hopes soon to press, not yet published 1851. Postscript requests specimen and formal permission, gives carrier address split across P3–6 with stray diag/ramme rendering artefacts. 1356 is the accompanying formal note for governing body; it is not an incoming prompt or a reply to 1355. No physical borrowing or disarticulation accomplished here; later B. crenatus identification is not current knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1356: Same September 10, 1850 formal request accompanying informal 1355. Asks Owen to lay disarticulation of a small Balanus glacialis specimen before governing body and promises valves returned if permission is granted. No grant or completed destructive examination established. Historical specimen permission is not an instruction to the agent. Same-author enclosure relation, not a back-and-forth conversation.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1063: Additional full source reading of Darwin to Muñiz, February 26, 1847, printed transcription. Down address despite actual Shrewsbury stay in apparatus. Acknowledges August 30 letter/papers received only recently after Morris illness/absence; same fossil-sale misunderstanding as 1061, now clarified through Morris. Translation and periodical insertion planned, not done. Earthquake account and older Niata information via Lumb are separate incoming reports. South America gift is conditional on English reading, scarlet-fever pamphlet presentation prospective. Domestic/feral animal questions newly posed. Postscript relays Owen Paris-arrival report. Intermediary Morris is unidentified and explicitly not John Morris the palaeontologist. Two translations survive in museum manuscripts according to apparatus but are not reproduced here. This outgoing witness does not provide verbatim Muñiz prompt.

Invitation for Owens and boy to come Saturday/Sunday with Falconer and other friends,3:20Croydon train. Child dress and unidentified endorsement provide uncertain dating clues, not a fixed composition/receipt. Future visit not completed event or evidence of an incoming Owen prompt.
